content.text: A maintenance plan is useful only if it is followed through. Before contractors {{gap:1}} out repairs, managers must inspect the equipment in service and check whether older components are likely to {{gap:2}} down under sustained pressure. They must also ask whether a hidden fault could {{gap:3}} up the schedule after work has begun. Teams may {{gap:4}} up against difficulties when a supplier changes specifications, while a delayed delivery can {{gap:5}} up an entire project whose deadlines were already narrow. For that reason, supervisors regularly {{gap:6}} into the plans rather than accepting optimistic estimates at face value. They {{gap:7}} out assumptions that no longer match the evidence and insist that each team {{gap:8}} through on its commitments, recording any revision so that the next shift understands what has changed and why. Such records make handovers safer because practical knowledge is preserved alongside the timetable, not left to whoever happens to remember the last decision.

questions.explanation: Carry out repairs means perform them.

distractorExplanations.B: Make repairs is possible, but carry out is the intended formal expression.
distractorExplanations.C: Take out repairs does not describe performing repairs.
distractorExplanations.D: Run out repairs is not idiomatic.

distractorExplanations.A: Fall down describes collapse, not a component ceasing to function.
distractorExplanations.C: Come down does not fit the intended meaning.
distractorExplanations.D: Wear down means gradually weaken, not fail suddenly.

distractorExplanations.B: Set up means arrange or establish, not delay a schedule.
distractorExplanations.C: Put up has several meanings but not this one in the sentence.
distractorExplanations.D: Take up would mean occupy time or space.

questions.explanation: Come up against difficulties means encounter them.

distractorExplanations.B: Bring up against is not idiomatic in this structure.
distractorExplanations.C: Put up against means place something next to or in opposition to something else.
distractorExplanations.D: Get up against is not the standard expression.

questions.explanation: Hold up the project means delay it.

distractorExplanations.B: Set up means establish, not delay.
distractorExplanations.C: Put up does not fit the object and meaning.
distractorExplanations.D: Keep up means maintain pace or standards, not cause delay.

questions.explanation: Look into the plans means investigate them.

distractorExplanations.B: Go into can mean discuss or enter a subject, but is not the intended collocation here.
distractorExplanations.C: Run into means encounter something unexpectedly.
distractorExplanations.D: Get into can mean become involved in something, not investigate it.

questions.explanation: Rule out means exclude from consideration.

distractorExplanations.B: Cross out means delete written text, not reject an assumption conceptually.
distractorExplanations.C: Cancel out means neutralise an effect.
distractorExplanations.D: Clear out means remove people or things physically.

questions.explanation: Follow through on commitments means do what was promised.

distractorExplanations.A: Carry through usually means complete something, but the preposition on points to follow through.
distractorExplanations.C: Keep through is not idiomatic in this structure.
distractorExplanations.D: Work through means deal with a problem, not honour a commitment.
